title: NSW launches pilot Joint Agency Cyber Command Centre with police and Cyber Security NSW
date_note: Both pages give only their publication day (24 November 2026); no earlier launch day is stated.
geo_basis: state government as the sources state it; pin placed at Sydney, the state capital, not stated by the pages
summary: The NSW Government, in a release republished by Mirage News, launched a pilot Joint Agency Cyber Command Centre where Cyber Security NSW staff are embedded with NSW Police Force cyber crime and cyber security teams. The pilot covers intelligence sharing, incident response and emergency management, and education and awareness. SecurityBrief Australia reports industry figures describe it as the first such arrangement by an Australian state government.
plain: New South Wales has started a pilot centre where state cyber security staff work alongside police cyber crime teams to share intelligence and respond to incidents.
exec: Government agencies in NSW get a joint police and cyber security team for sharing intelligence and handling incidents, according to the state's release.

validation.note: Mirage News (republishing the NSW Government release) and SecurityBrief Australia each state the launch of the joint centre; the NSW Government's own page was not read. The 'first by a state' description is from industry commentary in SecurityBrief only. ChannelLife, IT Brief and Techday carry the same story and count as one publisher with SecurityBrief.
